This package does not contain libstdc++. Unpacked every published alloy-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, 1.18.1-0 to 1.22.0-16, on amd64 and arm64 (1.21.2-0 was published for arm64 only); 87 packages, with no debug-symbol packages published for this source. Each holds one file, /usr/bin/alloy, a Go program built with cgo and dynamically linked against the system C library (libc.so.6 and its dynamic loader) and nothing else. No file is a copy of libstdc++, the program does not link libstdc++.so.6, and it carries no libstdc++ code: no GLIBCXX symbol versions and no basic_filebuf symbols. libstdc++ is shipped by the separate libstdc++6 package, built from the gcc-14 source, which is a different owner.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-125709 (GCC PR libstdc++/118099, https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=118099, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2569390): when basic_filebuf::overflow in libstdc++ fails to write its buffer after storing the overflow character, the put pointer is left past the end of the buffer, so repeated failing sputc() calls write further past it. It is fixed upstream on the GCC master branch by https://gcc.gnu.org/g:2d296e9f024edbb49cad1f3ebb5ae34c71ea5f7a, whose only library change is to basic_filebuf::overflow in bits/fstream.tcc (a guard that rewinds the put pointer when writing the buffer fails; the commit also adds tests), and on the releases/gcc-16 branch by its backport https://gcc.gnu.org/g:68b1b9056c70acb31f2964963b51c480ff820602. Two later master commits on the same bug report (https://gcc.gnu.org/g:43e4d697586364decbad7f67a204189afef6e765 and https://gcc.gnu.org/g:f46b50adcf752de0e1e0e24e17f42a5075770f48) avoid possible null pointer arithmetic with partial codecvt conversions in the unbuffered path and restructure the fix so the put pointer is not advanced before the write; the bug report records only the one releases/gcc-16 commit. No gcc-14 release has the fix, and the Debian security tracker lists trixie's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 as vulnerable (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-125709). The DHI gcc-14 packages for Debian 13 are rebuilt from Debian's 14.2.0-19 source and carry a backport of commit 2d296e9 from the fourth of the five 14.2.0-19 rebuilds in the DHI Debian repository on 2026-11-23. We checked libstdc++6, libstdc++-14-dev, libstdc++-14-pic and libstdc++6-14-dbg in all five rebuilds on amd64 and arm64, each verified against its index checksum, reading the symbol sizes of basic_filebuf<char>::overflow and basic_filebuf<wchar_t>::overflow in libstdc++.so.6, libstdc++.a and libstdc++_pic.a, with basic_filebuf<char>::xsputn as a control. In the first three rebuilds the two overflow functions are 542 and 570 bytes on amd64 and 524 and 512 bytes on arm64 in libstdc++6, libstdc++.a and libstdc++_pic.a (700 and 713, and 708 and 700, in the debug libraries of libstdc++6-14-dbg); in the fourth and fifth rebuilds they are 589 and 611 bytes on amd64 and 600 and 548 bytes on arm64 (764 and 777, and 756 and 748, in the debug libraries), while xsputn keeps its size in every rebuild. The bits/fstream.tcc header installed by libstdc++-14-dev contains the fix's guard in the fourth and fifth rebuilds and lacks it in the first three. The range ends at the fourth rebuild, the first published build with the fix.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-125709 is GCC bug libstdc++/118099: when std::basic_filebuf::overflow cannot write out its put area after storing the overflow character, it leaves the put pointer past the end of the buffer, and each further failed write stores further past it (https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=118099, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-125709). Upstream fixed it in libstdc++: https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/2d296e9f024edbb49cad1f3ebb5ae34c71ea5f7a. The code ships in the C++ standard library built from gcc-14 (the libstdc++6 package), which this package does not contain. Unpacked every published postgresql-15 build in the DHI Debian repository, each checked against the index SHA256: 15.19-1 and 15.2-0 on amd64 and arm64 (15.2-0 is PostgreSQL 15.20 by the version string of /usr/bin/postgres, although it sorts below 15.19-1); no debug-symbol packages are published for this source. Each build holds 122 programs and shared objects, all dynamically linked; 39 server modules on amd64 and 38 on arm64 list no libc.so.6 of their own (earthdistance.so needs only libm.so.6, sslinfo.so only libcrypto.so.3, the rest have no dependencies). The nine static archives (libpq.a, libecpg.a, libecpg_compat.a, libpgtypes.a, libpgport.a, libpgport_shlib.a, libpgcommon.a, libpgcommon_shlib.a and libpgfeutils.a, 180 members) hold PostgreSQL's own object files. No package contains a PE or Mach-O file or a jar, whl, zip or nupkg archive. The one file that uses the C++ standard library is the LLVM JIT provider llvmjit.so, which lists libLLVM.so.19.1, libstdc++.so.6 and libgcc_s.so.1 as dependencies and loads them from their own packages at run time. No package contains a copy of libstdc++, and the name basic_filebuf occurs in no file, llvmjit.so included. A fix for this CVE reaches this package's users through the libstdc++6 package, not through this one.

CVE-2026-125709 is in libstdc++, the GCC C++ standard library: when basic_filebuf::overflow fails to write its buffer, the put pointer is left past the end of the buffer and later writes overflow it (GCC PR libstdc++/118099, https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=118099, fixed upstream by https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/2d296e9f024edbb49cad1f3ebb5ae34c71ea5f7a; https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2569390, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-125709). This package does not contain libstdc++. Unpacked all 96 binary packages published from the postgresql-17 source in the DHI Debian repository, for amd64 and arm64: the rebuilds of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and 17.12-0+deb13u1 (postgresql-17, postgresql-client-17, postgresql-server-dev-17, postgresql-plperl-17, postgresql-plpython3-17, postgresql-pltcl-17, libpq5, libpq-dev, libecpg6, libecpg-dev, libecpg-compat3 and libpgtypes3, and their debug-symbol packages) and the 17.11-1 and 17.12-0 postgresql-17 packages. The programs, including the postgres server, and the client libraries are dynamically linked ELF files that list the system libc.so.6 in NEEDED. Some server extension modules, which are loaded into the postgres server process and resolve C library symbols from it, list no libc.so.6 of their own: in each rebuild of Debian's source, 27 with no NEEDED entries at all, earthdistance.so (whose one NEEDED entry is libm.so.6), bool_plperl.so (libperl, and on amd64 also the dynamic loader ld-linux-x86-64.so.2) and ltree_plpython3.so (libpython); in the 17.11-1 and 17.12-0 packages, 36 on amd64 and 35 on arm64 with no NEEDED entries, plus earthdistance.so and sslinfo.so (whose one NEEDED entry is libcrypto.so.3). The static archives shipped (libpq.a, libecpg.a, libecpg_compat.a, libpgtypes.a, libpgport.a, libpgport_shlib.a, libpgcommon.a, libpgcommon_shlib.a and libpgfeutils.a) hold PostgreSQL's own object files, and the debug-symbol packages hold detached debug information. No package contains a statically linked program, a PE file, a Mach-O file or a jar, whl, zip or nupkg archive. One file uses the C++ runtime: the LLVM JIT provider llvmjit.so in the postgresql-17 packages, which lists libLLVM.so.19.1, libstdc++.so.6 and libgcc_s.so.1 in NEEDED and loads them from the system at run time. No package contains a copy of libstdc++.so.6, libstdc++.a or libgcc_s, and the name basic_filebuf occurs in none of the ELF files or static archives in these packages, llvmjit.so included (which does contain other libstdc++ names such as basic_string). libstdc++ reaches an image through the packages built from the gcc-14 source (libstdc++6, libstdc++-14-dev, ...), which are not part of this owner and are assessed on their own.

CVE-2026-125709 is GCC bug libstdc++/118099: when std::basic_filebuf::overflow cannot write out its put area after storing the overflow character, it leaves the put pointer past the end of the buffer, and each further failed write stores further past it (https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=118099, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2569390). Upstream fixed it in libstdc++-v3/include/bits/fstream.tcc: https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/2d296e9f024edbb49cad1f3ebb5ae34c71ea5f7a. The code ships in the C++ standard library built from gcc-14 (the libstdc++6 package), which this package does not contain. Unpacked every published postgresql-18 build in the DHI Debian repository (18.6-1 and 18.7-0, on amd64 and arm64, each checked against the index SHA256; no debug-symbol packages are published for this source) and read every ELF file, including the members of its static archives: no file is, or bundles, a copy of libstdc++, and no ELF file defines std::basic_filebuf::overflow. The one ELF file that uses the C++ standard library is the LLVM JIT provider llvmjit.so, which links libstdc++.so.6 and libLLVM.so.19.1 dynamically from their own packages; no other ELF file links libstdc++. The static archives (libpq.a, libpq-oauth.a, libpgport.a, libpgport_shlib.a, libpgcommon.a, libpgcommon_shlib.a, libpgfeutils.a, libecpg.a, libecpg_compat.a and libpgtypes.a) hold PostgreSQL's own objects and no C++ standard library code. Any fix for this CVE reaches this package's users through the libstdc++6 package, not through this one.

CVE-2026-125709 is a flaw in libstdc++, the GNU C++ standard library built from GCC: when a byte-by-byte write fails during file stream processing, the stream buffer can still append data to its internal buffer, which can overflow it (https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-125709, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2569390). Unpacked every published python3-pip and python3-pip-whl package for Debian 13 from the DHI Debian repository: python3-pip 26.1.2dhi0, 26.1.2-0 to 26.1.2-4, 26.2-0, 26.2.1-0 to 26.2.1-2, 26.2.2-0 and 26.3-0, and python3-pip-whl 26.1.2-1 to 26.1.2-4, 26.2-0, 26.2.1-0 to 26.2.1-2, 26.2.2-0 and 26.3-0, all built for architecture all, including the contents of the pip wheel in python3-pip-whl. They contain pip's Python source; package metadata, license and other text data files, among them certifi's CA certificate bundle (cacert.pem) and a JavaScript worker file vendored with urllib3; the /usr/bin/pip and /usr/bin/pip3 Python scripts in python3-pip; and six Windows launcher programs from pip's vendored distlib (t32.exe, t64.exe, t64-arm.exe, w32.exe, w64.exe and w64-arm.exe), which are native Windows PE executables for x86, x86-64 and ARM64 with no .NET CLR header. No package contains an ELF file, a static archive or a Mach-O file. python3-pip ships no copy of libstdc++ and no compiled code that links against it; it runs on the Python interpreter that the image provides, which is assessed under its own packages.
